title: INNER JOIN
description: An INNER JOIN combines rows from two tables, keeping only the pairs where the join condition matches - rows with no match on either side are dropped entirely. Write a query that returns the customer's `first_name` and the order's `id` and `order_date`, for every customer that has placed at least one order.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: INNER JOIN

customers JOIN orders ON customers.id = orders.customer_id lines up each order with its customer - but a customer who has never ordered simply has no matching row on the orders side, so they won't appear in the result at all.
Join customers to orders on customers.id = orders.customer_id, then select first_name, orders.id, order_date.
expected_behavior: Returns one row per order, with the ordering customer's first_name alongside it - customers with zero orders are absent.
solution: SELECT customers.first_name, orders.id, orders.order_date FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.id = orders.customer_id;
explanation: JOIN with no qualifier means INNER JOIN - it's the default and the most common join, used whenever you only care about rows that exist on both sides of the relationship.
